evidence: A/schedule.png: the right panel puts alerts first, then a check-in checklist (Checked in, Insurance, Copay with a primary Collect $25.00 button, Room). The left rail has Waiting room / In a room / Due next with Check in buttons, and a 2× badge marks the 10:15 Feld double booking.

B/schedule.png: patient search is centred in the header. The left rail shows Waiting room with '$ copay due', In a room with minutes, Expected next with Check In buttons, Needs attention and Waitlist. The grid shows 8:00 to 1:30 PM with a 2× double-booking badge and a 'Now 8:04' marker.
before.png: 12 equal buttons in the right panel, and Patient Alerts sit below them.
before.png: grid names are truncated ('BRENNAN, HAROLD 75M F/...', 'JOHANSSON, MIA 4F 4yr sh...').
before.png: small all-caps text at about 11px throughout, and toolbar buttons and the search field look about 20px tall.

pairs.reason: A's selected panel turns check-in into a checklist with Collect copay as the primary action, and grid cells keep type as text (F/U, Sick). B leaves type mostly unlabelled.

notes: This was close. Both show status with text and icons rather than colour alone, pass contrast, and have no small targets. B's one contrast failure is a visually hidden 'Find patient' label (white on white), which no user sees, so I did not count it against primary text. B shows a longer span of the day and keeps the waitlist on screen. A's workflow for the 42% check-in task is sharper.
